ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $\angle B=46^\circ$, $\angle C=54^\circ$, $AD$ bisects $\angle BAC$, intersects $BC$ at $D$, and $DE\parallel AB$, intersecting $AC$ at $E$. What is the measure of $\angle ADE$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $\angle B=46^\circ$ and $\angle C=54^\circ$, \\
it follows that $\angle BAC=180^\circ-\angle B-\angle C=180^\circ-46^\circ-54^\circ=80^\circ$, \\
Since AD bisects $\angle BAC$, \\
it follows that $\angle BAD=\frac{1}{2}\angle BAC=40^\circ$, \\
Since DE $\parallel$ AB, \\
it follows that $\angle ADE=\angle BAD=\boxed{40^\circ}$.
